# Service case study — private evidence before public claims

Template only; no customer/project/result is asserted. Store the completed raw worksheet outside Git. Only a separately reviewed, sanitized case with explicit consent may become public WordPress content.

| Required field | Private working value |
|---|---|
| Owner and reviewer | UNASSIGNED |
| Customer publication consent | NOT_GRANTED |
| Allowed brand/logo/name scope | NONE |
| Service owner URL and actual delivered scope | TO_VERIFY |
| Before observation, date, device/method and evidence locator | TO_VERIFY |
| Changes authorized and actually made | TO_VERIFY |
| After observation with comparable method/conditions | TO_VERIFY |
| Unresolved limits, other changes and uncertainty | REQUIRED |
| Customer acceptance and wording approval | NOT_GRANTED |
| Secret/customer-data/media-rights review | PENDING |
| Publication state | PRIVATE_DRAFT |

Publication gate: verified evidence, comparable observations, explicit owner/customer consent, rights for every image, technical review and privacy guard. Remove access details, raw logs, customer identifiers and exact operational addresses. Describe correlation as observation; do not claim a causal improvement without suitable evidence. Never fill missing fields with fictional clients, logos, metrics, ratings, certifications or SLA.

An educational hypothetical scenario can be published as such, but must not be labeled a real case study. The proposed support engagement patterns on the service page are negotiation options, not approved rates or SLA tiers. Existing ticket history remains the request system of record; this worksheet creates no parallel customer backend.
